set.frame: the pole hall: origin at its floor centre (y 0); bearings clockwise from north (Roblox -Z). CFrame = CFrame.new(position) * CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(yawDeg), 0).

redRoom.placement: client-local, one per player: under the player's own bay, origin = bay origin + (0, -40, 0), same yaw (its roof top then sits 18 studs under the hall floor). Nobody else ever sees it.
redRoom.liftTravel: the rose lift disc rises from y 0.15 up through the hex frame (y 21.6) into the dark above the roof; the cut to the case hides there

rise.bayFrame: relative to the case bay's CFrame (origin = bay floor centre, LookVector = toward the hall centre); multiply by the bay's CFrame for world positions

endFrame.reference: the film's low-angle, whole-body frame (T1 @127.2 s): in front of the rider, just below the disc, looking up past the body to the pole

full.profile: accelerate 2.0 s, cruise 5.0 s at 17.14 studs/s, brake 2.0 s
full.orbitDirection: anticlockwise seen from above; 90 = in front of the rider (toward the hall centre), 180 = the rider's left, 270 = behind

short.profile: accelerate 1.6 s, cruise 2.0 s at 34.29 studs/s, brake 1.4 s
short.orbitDirection: anticlockwise seen from above; 90 = in front of the rider (toward the hall centre), 180 = the rider's left, 270 = behind

rise.profile: accelerate 2.0 s, cruise 5.0 s at 17.14 studs/s, brake 2.0 s
rise.orbitDirection: anticlockwise seen from above; 90 = in front of the rider (toward the hall centre), 180 = the rider's left, 270 = behind

sequence.rule: TwoArenas 2.3: the full cut if any contender in the round has not launched yet this session, else the short cut; everyone in a round sees the same cut on the same clock

full.stage: Fade to black on the training floor
1 The red room (loops while the arena streams in)
full.camera: just above the hex frame's mouth (Blender (0, 2, 30), 7.5 studs over the frame), looking 75 deg down past the far half of the hexagon at the player's own stand-in on the lift disc (Spawn) far below, in the oxblood hood; a slow zoom, fov 50 -> 42 over 6 s, then a 4 deg/s drift if the wait runs on. At 6 s the player looks up into the tube.
rises ahead of the player through the hex frame into the dark above the roof (hidden cut 1)

at face height just outside the glass, beside the player, looking past the player (who turns toward the row) along the tightly packed row of cases with a long lens (35 mm on 36 mm film, about 54 deg across; cameraStart, in the bay frame); then pulls back and arcs 40 deg round the hall, ending in front of the case at rise.cuts.full.keys[0]

a whole turn anticlockwise from the front while climbing with the rider; from t 5.4 it settles into the film's low-angle, whole-body frame (rise.endFrame, T1 @127.2 s), held from t 6.8 while the rider is still in the open hall; the opening floods white from t 7.4

full.stage: 5 White-out (the cut into the arena hides here)

full.camera: out of the white 14 studs above the plinth, looking down (T1 @129.2 s); drops behind the head facing the horn, then into first person at 28.0. The rise now ends in front of the rider, so reaching 'behind the head' is a further half turn, not pass 1's quarter.

short.stage: 1 The red room, only as long as loading needs

short.camera: a cut straight to the disc leaving the case, seen from behind and to the right (clear of the gantry behind the cases); 155 deg anticlockwise to the same low-angle end frame by t 3.4, held; floods white from t 4.2

lighting.note: pass 2 (TwoArenas 2.8) with the review's fixes: the hue rides on the light, not the paint. Cool keys and a navy ambient in both halls and blue keys over the deck turn the shadows blue; the red room keeps one cool white key down the tube and red light only in its two floor openings. Neon parts light nothing (as in Roblox): every light below is a real Light. Light colours are 0-1 RGB (Light.Color), gains are the Blender watts of the previews (relative only), ambients and exposures as Lighting.Ambient and ExposureCompensation. The values were set on the Blender previews (paint x ambient, AgX, the bloom and atmosphere stand-ins below) and measured with tools/art/colour_band.py (tools/art/specs/launch.json); confirm them in Studio (ArtStyle rule 10) before shipping.

LaunchRedRoom.lights: SpotLight at KeyLight (coolWhite, angle 13, aimed down the tube onto the lift disc only); SpotLights at DeckKey_1-4 (deckKey, angle 54, leaning in toward the grate lanes: they make the neutral steel deck read blue); a coolKey SpotLight (angle 26) at WalkwaySpot, over the walkway; a dim navy SurfaceLight (Face Bottom, grateGlow) under each grate lane's mesh at GrateGlow_1-4, so the voids read navy-black; a red SurfaceLight (Face Top) low in each floor opening at OpeningGlow_1-2, the only red light; white SpotLights (lampLight, angle 50, tipped 10 deg down) at Lamp_n, the way each lamp faces

LaunchCaseHall.lights: a SurfaceLight (Face Bottom, Angle 50, coolWhite) on each case top-light, aimed at the disc; SurfaceLights (Face Bottom, caseStageGantry) on the gantry strips; a small SurfaceLight on each unit panel. While the cases stage runs, the pole hall's hub spots are off and its bars take caseStageBars at caseStageDim of their gains

atmosphere.note: a thin navy haze (Lighting.Atmosphere in this profile): the preview blends toward the colour with distance

LaunchPoleHall.lights: SpotLights (angle 34, poleHallBars) at the 12 HubSpot_n, which hang in two tiers under the hub; a SurfaceLight (Face Bottom) on every ceiling-ring LED bar and one (Face Front, toward the hall centre) on every wall bar; no light on the poles; a SpotLight that rides 7 studs in front of and 10 above each rider (the rider key, coolWhite). Phones: only the own rider's key and the 4 nearest; Low graphics drops the wall bars' lights

LaunchPoleHallRise.note: the rise's own profile: as the camera settles into the low-angle end frame the pole hall's ambient blends to this greyer navy, the bars take riseBars and the exposure eases (rise.cuts.*.keys[].riseProfile and .exposure), so the lit rider stands out against a hall that falls away (T1 @127.2 s)

import: Import each GLB (3D Importer). Each asset root arrives as a Model of MeshParts named <Asset>_<Part>.
Re-centre each asset: Model.WorldPivot = CFrame.new(origin), then PivotTo(CFrame.new()).
Per part from the manifest: Material = robloxMaterial, Color = rgb, CanCollide = collide, CollisionFidelity = collision, CastShadow, CanQuery, CanTouch, Transparency; Anchored = true.

Paint parts: one SurfaceAppearance per part (ColorMap, RoughnessMap, MetalnessMap from the upload files of its textureSet; no NormalMap). Neon parts: Material Neon, no SurfaceAppearance. Glass: Material Glass, Transparency 0.65, Reflectance 0.2. Collider: Transparency 1.
Build the set from set.instances in a folder far from the arena; it is client-side (clone it on the client for the launch). The red room is cloned per player under their own bay.
Attachments: create under the asset's main part with WorldCFrame = pivot * CFrame.lookAt(position, position + look, up).
The palette textures are nearest-colour cells (8 px); the cells are sorted by colour so mips stay clean.
styleRules: Style A: chunky volumes at true scale, flat facets, built members as chamfered prisms; nothing under 0.25 stud except bolts and trim.

Colour: the brief's semi-real tones (UpcomingFilm_Brief section 2.8), +-6% per volume, +-3% per facet, warm tops and cool undersides, AO >= 0.5; each surface's mean after AO is normalised to the tone. The reds sit at their frame sample's saturation (within 0.05; palette.redCheck); saturated colour only on the light sources.
Darkness comes from the lighting, never the paint: no painted value below luma 40 (grates); built surfaces 55-215.
